Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
articles.full_content:
Event highlights the pivotal role of women farmers in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra highlights invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors; emphasises the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, celebrated Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 today (15 October 2026 ) at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The programme was organised to recognise the invaluable contribution of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their pivotal role in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Sh. Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in his address, highlighted the invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors, particularly in ensuring food security, sustaining rural livelihoods, managing natural resources and driving agricultural development. He emphasised the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture through various initiatives, including direct income support, affordable institutional credit, technology transfer, skill development, farm mechanisation and improved access to agricultural marketing infrastructure.

Ministry of Coal Accelerates Cleanliness And E- Waste Management efforts Under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Coal is intensifying efforts to advance cleanliness, efficient space utilisation and responsible waste management across its offices and public sector undertakings under the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6
As part of the campaign, an e-waste collection drive was organised at a dedicated kiosk in the Main Entrance Lobby of GPOA-3, New Delhi. Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey participated in the drive by depositing discarded electronic items at the kiosk. The activity highlighted the importance of responsible e-waste disposal, systematic collection and scientific recycling in promoting environmental sustainability and resource efficiency.
To review the progress of the campaign, the Ministry of Coal convened a meeting with Nodal Officers from Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited (NLCIL), Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO). The meeting assessed the status of ongoing activities and emphasised the need to expedite implementation, maintain momentum and complete all identified tasks within the stipulated timelines. Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal called upon the participating organisations to intensify their efforts and ensure the timely achievement of campaign targets.
Under Special Campaign 6, CPSEs under the Ministry of Coal have made notable progress in cleanliness and space management, with 562 sites cleaned and transformed by the midpoint of the implementation phase. These efforts reflect a sustained commitment to improving workplace environments, eliminating unused and cluttered spaces, and promoting better utilisation of infrastructure across offices and field establishments.
ECL undertook a comprehensive cleaning and beautification drive across 15,000 sq. ft. in Pandaveswar Area. The activity involved the removal of wild vegetation, bushes, weeds and accumulated debris, significantly improving the cleanliness, safety and appearance of the premises.
WCL: The Security Department at WCL Headquarters transformed an underutilised space into a modern, well-organised Corporate Security Office under Special Campaign 6. The initiative demonstrates the effective utilisation of existing infrastructure to create a more functional and organised workplace.
Through these concerted efforts, the Ministry of Coal and its CPSEs are advancing the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0 by combining cleanliness drives, scientific waste management and the productive use of available spaces. The campaign continues to reinforce a culture of cleanliness, accountability and operational efficiency across the coal sector.

• Overall UR (15+ years) remained stable at 5.0% in September 2026, down by 0.2 percentage points from September 2025.
• Rural Female UR declined by 0.4 percentage points year-on-year to 3.9% in September 2026, the lowest level recorded during 2026.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on labour force participation and employment and unemployment conditions. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status [1] (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to August, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for September, 2026 is the eighteenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
• Rise in urban Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 55.5% in September, 2026, compared to 55.6% in August, 2026. In rural areas, LFPR was recorded at 58.0% against 58.2% in August, 2026, while the urban LFPR registered a moderate increase of 0.3 percentage points, rising from 50.4% in August, 2026 to 50.7% in September, 2026.
Over the year, the overall LFPR increased by 0.2 percentage points, from 55.3% in September, 2025 to 55.5% in September, 2026. During the same period, rural LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 57.4% to 58.0%, while urban LFPR registered a marginal decline of 0.2 percentage points, from 50.9% to 50.7%.

articles.title: NITI Aayog’s Frontier Tech Hub Unveils Data Centre Evaluation Framework to Help States Plan for Sustainable Growth
articles.full_content:
Framework aims to help States move from attracting data-centre investments to building investment-ready infrastructure, protecting critical resources and maximising long-term economic value
NITI Aayog’s Frontier Tech Hub has released the Data Centre Evaluation Framework on 14 October 2026 to help States plan for sustainable growth of data centres. The release took place in the presence of Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog; Shri Anurag Jain, CEO, NITI Aayog; Ms Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog; representatives from the Ministry of Power, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) , Ministry of Commerce; as well as representatives from industry and the media.
The Framework, developed with inputs from industry, MeitY, Ministry of Power and DPIIT, provides State governments with a practical approach to planning, evaluating and facilitating data-centre investments. It helps them assess infrastructure readiness, safeguard critical resources and maximise long-term economic and strategic value.
India’s data-centre capacity has grown from about 375 MW in 2020 to approximately 1.5 GW currently, driven by the growing demand for Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud computing, high-performance computing and data-intensive digital applications.
As India accelerates its AI and digital transformation, data centres are emerging as critical infrastructure underpinning the country's technological and economic ambitions. While this presents a significant opportunity, data centres at increasing scale also place substantial demands on electricity, water, land, connectivity and local infrastructure. The focus therefore needs to move beyond attracting investment to ensuring that projects are developed in locations where the necessary infrastructure and resources can support them over the long term.
The Government of India has taken important steps to create an enabling environment for data-centre investments, including a tax holiday until 2047 for eligible foreign cloud service providers leveraging India-based data-centre infrastructure. As investments grow in scale, effective State-level planning and investment readiness will be critical to ensuring sustainable growth of the sector.
Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog, highlighted the opportunity to leverage data-centre investments to build India’s technological capabilities. He emphasised the need to strengthen domestic R&D, industry–academia collaboration and Indian participation across the data-centre technology value chain. He also underscored the potential for India to develop innovative solutions in advanced cooling, energy efficiency and resource-efficient computing, converting infrastructure investments into long-term economic and technological value.

The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS. Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), and Senior Officers from DDWS were also present during the Samvad.
In his opening remarks, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS , said that this platform has emerged as an important platform for peer learning, enabling district administrations to share innovative practices and address implementation challenges in rural drinking water service delivery. He emphasised the pivotal role of District Collectors in strengthening local water governance, ensuring effective operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems, and promoting community ownership of assets created under the Mission.
Secretary, DDWS calls for Greater Accountability and Data-Driven Governance. He directed districts to ensure regular monthly meetings of District Water and Sanitation Missions (DWSMs) and timely uploading of meeting minutes on the DWSM Portal. He stressed that strong institutional monitoring and documentation are essential for transparency, accountability and effective programme implementation.

Kolkata, October 15, 2026
Celebrating the invaluable contributions of rural women to agriculture, fisheries and wetland-based livelihoods, ICAR-Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CIFRI), Barrackpore, observed Mahila Kisan Diwas at Bartir Beel, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, today, coinciding with the International Day of Rural Women. The programme highlighted women’s empowerment, gender equality and the potential of sustainable fisheries and responsible eco-aqua tourism to create new livelihood opportunities. Known locally as the “Dal Lake of Bengal’’, Bartir Beel is a seasonal floodplain wetland rich in aquatic biodiversity. Supporting indigenous fish, snails, crabs and diverse birdlife, the wetland also sustains seasonal agriculture as floodwaters recede. Its ecological richness and livelihood potential make it a promising landscape for integrating sustainable fisheries, wetland conservation and community-based tourism. The programme brought together 30 women farmers and rural resource users, recognising their significant contributions to agriculture, fisheries and local economic activities. Women play an important role in Rabi-season onion cultivation, undertaking nursery management, weeding, harvesting, sorting and marketing-related activities. They also contribute to jute processing, including fibre stripping, washing, sorting and drying, while participating in wetland-based livelihoods and local trade. Despite their substantial contributions, social barriers and taboos often limit women’s participation in emerging opportunities, particularly eco-aqua tourism. The interactions underscored the need for targeted capacity building, access to scientific knowledge and improved technologies, institutional support, and greater representation of women in community-level planning and decision-making. Dr. B. K. Behere, Chief Executive Officer, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), graced the occasion as Chief Guest and emphasised the critical role of rural women in fisheries, aquaculture and livelihood development. Highlighting the principle that “Empowering women is empowering entire humanity,” he stressed that women’s empowerment is central to enhancing fish production, household nutritional security and rural well-being. Dr. Pradip Dey, Director, ICAR-CIFRI, envisioned transforming Bartir Beel into a model of women-led, science-based and ecologically sustainable rural development, recognising rural women as key stakeholders, knowledge holders and entrepreneurs.He emphasised integrating scientific fisheries management, biodiversity conservation, value addition and eco-aqua tourism to diversify livelihoods, strengthen nutritional security and generate dignified employment for women and rural youth. BIS Dehradun Celebrates World Standards Day 2026 with Focus on Affordable and Clean Energy
articles.full_content:
Special emphasis on the role of Indian standards in affordable & clean energy and sustainable development More than 200 participants from industry, trade associations and other stakeholder organisations attend the event
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Dehradun Branch Office, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 at Hotel Regenta, Mohabbewala, Dehradun, with a special focus on this year’s theme, “Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7): Affordable and Clean Energy.” The event witnessed the participation of more than 200 representatives from industry, trade associations, the jewellery sector, BIS licensees and other stakeholders.
Shri Saurabh Thapliyal, Mayor of Dehradun, attended the programme as the Chief Guest. Smt. Ruchi Mohan Rayal, Additional Secretary, Food and Civil Supplies Department, was present as the Guest of Honour. Shri Anupam Dwivedi, Joint Director, Department of Industries, also attended the event. Representatives from the Indian Industries Association (IIA), Industries Association of Uttarakhand, PHDCCI and UIWA participated in the programme, reflecting the collective commitment of industry and other stakeholders towards quality and sustainable development.
The programme highlighted the vital role of Indian Standards in promoting affordable and clean energy, improving energy efficiency, encouraging renewable energy technologies and supporting environmentally sustainable industrial practices. The discussions emphasised that the effective implementation of quality standards is essential for ensuring reliable, safe and energy-efficient products while contributing to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
Experts from Exide, Microtek, Novateur and Mochiko delivered detailed presentations on various aspects of affordable and clean energy. Their presentations covered technological developments, energy-efficient solutions and the importance of quality and standardisation in advancing sustainable energy practices. The sessions provided valuable insights into the role of industry in developing and adopting solutions that support a cleaner and more sustainable future.

First, jobs require ecosystems, not isolated interventions. Sustainable job creation requires high-quality and inclusive economic growth, which in turn needs macroeconomic stability, efficient infrastructure, simple and certain regulations, and broad-based access to finance and skills. Guarantees and risk mitigation instruments are among the most effective tools to accelerate risk-capital formation and crowding in private capital.

The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, held a two-day National Workshop on “Strengthening Digital Data Systems and Evidence-Based Learning” under DAY-NRLM, on 12th and 13th October 2026, at Gurugram, Haryana. Representatives of State Rural Livelihoods Missions, NITI Aayog, the World Bank, GIZ, J-PAL, Gates Foundation, 3ie, BRAC, NABARD, NPCI, financial institutions and development partners participated in the workshop.
In his keynote address, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, GoI, said that around 10 crore women organised into nearly 92 lakh SHGs have leveraged formal credit of about ₹14 lakh crore. The next phase must strengthen around 87 lakh enterprises and track the progress of Lakhpati Didis towards the target of six crore. He said “what gets measured gets done; what gets measured gets improved,” and called for LokOS to become an operational platform integrated with banking portals for a seamless digital credit journey. The ICAR–Central Institute for Women in Agriculture (ICAR-CIWA), Bhubaneswar, commemorated Rashtriya Mahila Kisan Diwas today, aligning with the global observance of the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026. The convention brought together over 250 participants—including women farmers, Self-Help Group (SHG) members, Women Farmer Producer Organizations (WFPOs), students, and agricultural scientists—to recognize and advance the role of women in agriculture.
Welcoming the delegates, Dr. Mridula Devi, Director of ICAR-CIWA, highlighted the institute’s commitment to developing gender-responsive technologies, building capacity, and creating sustainable livelihood models. She emphasized that targeted skill training, technology transfer, and institutional support are essential to enhancing farm productivity and expanding rural women's entrepreneurship.
Chief Guest Shri Sachin Ramchandra Jadhav, IAS, Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Empowerment, Government of Odisha, stressed that closing the gender gap and ensuring equal opportunity are vital to realizing the sector's full potential. He commended ICAR-CIWA for formulating state-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for farm machinery, enabling women farmers to operate equipment safely and independently. Shri Jadhav also called for collaborative policy interventions between ICAR-CIWA and the state government to strengthen women’s land rights. Guest of Honour Prof. S. Pasupalak, Former Vice-Chancellor of OUAT, urged women farmers to leverage collective group action and highlighted the importance of impact assessments for women-friendly agricultural implements.
A major milestone of the celebration was the distribution of ICAR-CIWA’s pedal-operated coconut dehusker to 50 women SHGs to mitigate physical drudgery, prevent occupational hazards, and enhance household incomes. Participants also explored dynamic demonstrations of farm innovations, including agricultural drones, the Integrated Vertical Nutri Farming System (IVNFS), hydroponics, mushroom cultivation, disc ridgers, and maize dehusker-cum-shellers.
The event honored six progressive women farmers for their exceptional contributions to agricultural production and allied enterprises. The day concluded with an interactive scientist–farmer interface focused on climate-resilient farming practices, improved crop varieties, and modern farm management strategies.

NABARD subscribes ₹4 Crore to NSDC's Social Stock Exchange Issue to support overseas employment of rural youth
articles.full_content:
Mumbai : 14 October 2026
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) has fully subscribed ₹4 crore to the maiden Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) issue of the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) platform of the National Stock Exchange (NSE), marking an important milestone in the evolution of outcome-based social finance in India. The project, with an estimated outlay of ₹11.25 crore, seeks to create sustainable overseas employment opportunities for 600 rural youth belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in Madhya Pradesh.
The initiative is being implemented by NSDC in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh and is structured around an innovative financing framework that aligns funding with measurable social outcomes. Under the model, NABARD is participating through its subscription to the ZCZP issue, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh is expected to provide outcome-linked funding of ₹5.60 crore upon the achievement of agreed employment outcomes. The remaining funding is proposed to come through beneficiary contributions.
The programme aims to equip rural youth with internationally relevant skills required for employment opportunities in Japan and Germany. Beneficiaries will receive language training, technical skill development, certification, cultural orientation and end-to-end support for overseas placement, including documentation and deployment assistance. The initiative seeks to create sustainable livelihood opportunities and improve income prospects for rural households through access to global labour markets.
A distinctive feature of the project is its emphasis on outcomes rather than activities. The programme is designed to focus on verified overseas employment and sustained livelihood enhancement rather than merely on the completion of training. This approach represents an important shift towards evidence-based development financing, with social impact remaining central to programme design and implementation.
The transaction also demonstrates the growing potential of the Social Stock Exchange as a platform for mobilising resources towards measurable developmental outcomes. Established under the regulatory framework of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the SSE seeks to facilitate greater participation by institutions, philanthropies, foundations, corporates and other stakeholders in financing social initiatives through transparent and accountable mechanisms. The ZCZP instrument is one such innovation that enables the funding of social projects without creating repayment obligations for implementing entities.
NABARD's participation reflects its commitment to strengthening the Social Stock Exchange ecosystem and exploring innovative financing mechanisms capable of addressing complex rural development challenges. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman to embark on an official visit to Bangkok, Thailand, from 14th to 18th October 2026

Union Finance Minister to attend Annual Meetings of the IMF-World Bank FM will also take part in G20 and G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) meetings besides bilateral meetings with many countries and organisations Smt. Sitharaman will participate in multilateral dialogues on various fora to showcase India’s economic dynamism
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will undertake an official visit to Bangkok, Thailand, from October 14th to 18th, 2026, to participate in the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, along with meetings of the G20 and G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG).
During the visit, the Union Finance Minister will participate in a series of multilateral meetings and discussions on key global economic and financial issues, including current economic developments and financial sector issues. These engagements will provide an opportunity to exchange perspectives on the global economic outlook, development priorities and international financial cooperation.
The Union Finance Minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with H.E. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of the Kingdom of Thailand; and the Finance Ministers of Switzerland, Japan, Luxembourg, Bhutan and Curaçao.
She will also meet Ms. Kristalina Georgieva; Managing Director of the IMF; and Governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC).
In addition to the ministerial engagements, Smt. Sitharaman will participate in discussions and events involving global policymakers, financial institutions and other stakeholders. These include an Atlantic Council fire-side chat on India’s growth outlook, trade resilience and outreach, reform of the international financial architecture, India and the ASEAN, and the road to Viksit Bharat 2047 among the topics; and a Germany side event on Working Together to Make Cities Investable – Mobilising Private Capital for Urban and Water Infrastructure.
The engagements will provide a platform to highlight India’s economic performance, reform priorities and investment opportunities, while strengthening dialogue and cooperation with international partners on issues of global economic significance.
The visit underscores India’s active engagement with multilateral institutions and its commitment to constructive international cooperation on global economic and financial challenges.

CSTARI Kolkata and IIT Kharagpur Sign MoU to Strengthen Vocational Education and Skill Development
articles.full_content:
Kolkata: October 14, 2026
The Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI), Kolkata, under the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), has signed yesterday a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to strengthen the quality, relevance and effectiveness of vocational education and training in India.
The MoU was signed by Professor Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur and Shri Rajnish Kumar Jha, Director, CSTARI, marking an important step towards fostering institutional collaboration by integrating academic excellence, research and technological innovation with expertise in vocational training.
The partnership aims to promote research-driven and technology-enabled approaches to enhance trainer effectiveness, improve teaching–learning practices and strengthen training outcomes. Key areas of collaboration include pedagogy and instructional design, technology-enabled learning, digital content and curriculum development, computer-based assessment, evaluation and certification systems, faculty development, and Training of Trainers (ToT).
The collaboration will also focus on research and innovation in vocational education and skill development, industry–institute partnerships for curriculum validation, joint projects, knowledge exchange, workshops and capacity-building initiatives. The institutions may undertake additional mutually agreed activities to advance their shared objectives.
The MoU provides a framework for leveraging IIT Kharagpur’s academic and research capabilities alongside CSTARI’s expertise in training methodology, curriculum development and capacity building. The partnership is expected to contribute to improved instructional practices, enhanced trainer competencies and the continuous improvement of vocational education and training.

Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 to Be Celebrated at the National Level Tomorrow by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
articles.full_content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, is organising the national-level celebration of Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 on 15 October 2026 at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The programme aims to recognise and honour the significant contributions of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their role in advancing agricultural development and building a Viksit Bharat. The day also coincides with the International Day of Rural Women, established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, highlighting the contribution of rural women to agricultural and rural development.
Women are an integral part of India's agricultural system. From sowing, transplanting and harvesting to livestock management, seed conservation, natural resource management and value addition, women contribute significantly across the agricultural value chain. Their traditional knowledge, role in biodiversity conservation, entrepreneurial initiatives and adoption of sustainable agricultural practices are vital to strengthening rural livelihoods and enhancing agricultural resilience. As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, females constituted 59.8% of the total workforce engaged in agricultural activities during January–December 2025.
The year 2026 has been declared the International Year of the Woman Farmer (IYWF 2026) by the United Nations, providing an important global platform to recognise the contributions of women farmers to agrifood systems and promote their empowerment. The observance further underscores the need to enhance opportunities for women in agriculture and strengthen their access to resources, technology and institutional support.
The theme for Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 is “Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India.” The theme highlights the leadership of women in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat through the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, crop diversification, livestock management, and conservation of natural resources and the development of agriculture-based enterprises. Women farmers are contributing to making agriculture more productive, sustainable and self-reliant.
The programme will bring together outstanding women farmers from various States and Union Territories, along with women agricultural officers, agricultural extension functionaries and officers and officials of DA&FW. It will provide a platform to recognise their achievements, facilitate the sharing of experiences and successful practices and encourage greater participation and leadership of women across the agricultural sector.
